steps.title: Overview of what gets set up
steps.explain: Jobber needs a few accounts and a few settings before it can run. This guide goes through them one at a time, names each setting and says what it is for, and never asks you for a value. You enter values yourself in the setup wizard or in your own editor.

steps.title: Machine prerequisites
steps.explain: These are the programs Jobber runs on: Node.js, tmux, the Telegram bridge, and Chrome for the browser sessions. Missing ones are installed by the bootstrap script, which asks before it changes anything.

fixes.bootstrap_complete: Run bash scripts/bootstrap.sh in your own terminal and answer its questions.
fixes.node-version: Install a newer Node.js, then run the bootstrap script again.
fixes.tmux: Install tmux (the bootstrap script offers this), then run the doctor again.
fixes.chrome: Install Google Chrome. It is needed for the LinkedIn and Naukri browser sessions.
fixes.browser-binaries: Run npm ci to install the patchright package. Browsers run on the installed Google Chrome, so no browser download is needed.
fixes.ccgram-version: Install the exact ccgram version pinned in config/ccgram.pin.json using the bootstrap script.

steps.title: Claude Code login
steps.explain: Jobber drives Claude Code with your own subscription, so the claude program must be installed and logged in. Logging in opens a browser page that only you can complete.

fixes.claude-cli: Install Claude Code, then start it once with the claude command.
fixes.claude-login: Run claude in your own terminal and finish the browser login.

steps.title: Telegram bot and bridge

keys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
keys.purpose: token of your own bot, from BotFather

keys.name: ALLOWED_USERS
keys.purpose: numeric Telegram user ids allowed to talk to the bot

steps.explain: Telegram is how Jobber reports to you and takes commands. You create the bot yourself in BotFather and turn on threaded mode. The wizard stores the bot token and your user id.

fixes.telegram-api: Create the bot with BotFather per docs/telegram-bot-setup.md and run the wizard step again.
fixes.ccgram-env: Run the wizard telegram step so the token and allowed user id are stored.
fixes.daemon: Start the bridge with bash scripts/ccgram/start.sh in your own terminal.

steps.skip: Skippable (RECOMMENDED). If skipped: no phone control, no Telegram alerts, and no approved email follow-ups. Doctor shows telegram-api, ccgram-env and daemon as skipped.

steps.title: Gmail sending

keys.name: GMAIL_OAUTH_PATH
keys.purpose: path of the Google OAuth client file

keys.name: GMAIL_CREDENTIALS_PATH
keys.purpose: path where the Gmail login token is stored

keys.name: GMAIL_USER
keys.purpose: legacy SMTP address, unused with the OAuth server

keys.name: GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD
keys.purpose: legacy SMTP app password, unused with the OAuth server

steps.explain: Cold emails go out through your own Gmail using a Google OAuth client you create. The consent screen is a browser page only you can approve. The client file and the token live in secrets/ and never leave your machine.

fixes.gmail-oauth: Follow docs/gmail-mcp-setup.md to create the OAuth client and approve consent, then run the wizard step again.

steps.skip: Skippable (NEEDED FOR EMAIL OUTREACH). If skipped: no cold email, no email follow-ups, no reply watching; LinkedIn and Naukri outreach still run. Doctor shows gmail-oauth as skipped.

steps.title: Optional API keys (Serper and Hunter for contact finding)

keys.name: SERPER_API_KEY
keys.purpose: Serper search key for contact finding

keys.name: HUNTER_API_KEY
keys.purpose: Hunter key for contact finding, last-resort email lookup

keys.name: HUNTER_ENABLED
keys.purpose: whether Hunter lookups are allowed

keys.name: HUNTER_MONTHLY_CAP
keys.purpose: Hunter credits allowed per month

keys.name: DORK_ENABLED
keys.purpose: whether contact finding may search through the browser first

keys.name: DORK_BLOCK_COOLDOWN_HOURS
keys.purpose: hours the browser search stays off after a block

keys.name: SEARCH_CACHE_TTL_DAYS
keys.purpose: days a contact-finding search result is reused

keys.name: SERPER_DAILY_BUDGET
keys.purpose: Serper searches allowed per day for contact finding

keys.name: SERPER_MONTHLY_BUDGET
keys.purpose: Serper searches allowed per month for contact finding

keys.name: DORK_DAILY_BUDGET
keys.purpose: browser searches allowed per day for contact finding

steps.explain: Two optional services: Serper (contact finding) and Hunter (contact finding, last-resort email lookup, off unless you confirm). Each can be skipped and added later. Keys are typed hidden into the wizard and never shown. Skipping only records the choice.

fixes.api-keys: Run the wizard apikeys step to add the keys you want, or leave them unset; this is a warning only.

steps.skip: Skippable per key (OPTIONAL). Serper off: fewer verified contacts (contact finding). Hunter off: last-resort email lookup stays off. Doctor shows api-keys as skipped.

steps.title: LinkedIn and Naukri sessions

keys.name: APPLY_ALLOW_ACCOUNT_CREATION
keys.purpose: whether the applier may create accounts on apply sites (ships false)

keys.name: APPLY_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_HOSTS
keys.purpose: whether the applier may drive a host that is not a known ATS (ships false)

keys.name: APPLY_LINKEDIN_EASY
keys.purpose: whether LinkedIn Easy Apply through the burner account is allowed (ships false)

keys.name: APPLY_SUBMIT_MODE
keys.purpose: hold (default) stops the browser applier at the review step; submit really clicks submit

keys.name: APPLY_MAX_STEPS
keys.purpose: most next, back and save clicks one browser application may make (default 12)

keys.name: APPLY_RECIPE_PROMOTE_N
keys.purpose: confirmed submitted applications needed before a learned ATS recipe is written (default 3)

keys.name: APPLY_RECIPE_PROMOTE_RUNS
keys.purpose: distinct run ids those confirmed applications must span before a learned ATS recipe is written (default 2)

keys.name: APPLY_HOST_COOLDOWN_DAYS
keys.purpose: days a host is not opened by the browser applier after two blocks within 7 days (default 7)

keys.name: APPLY_SCREENSHOT
keys.purpose: whether the applier offers a screenshot tool; its pixels are not injection-screened (on by default, set false to disable)

keys.name: SCOUT_ALLOW_SIGNUP
keys.purpose: whether the scout may create accounts on discovery sites (ships false)

keys.name: SITE_MAIL_VERIFY
keys.purpose: how sign-up verification links arrive: owner_assist (default), gmail or off

keys.name: SITE_MAIL_SENDERS
keys.purpose: sender addresses whose verification mail may be read in gmail mode (empty by default)

keys.name: APPLY_ACCEPT_LEGAL_REQUIRED
keys.purpose: whether a required privacy or terms box may be checked to submit (marketing boxes never are)

keys.name: LINKEDIN_ACCEPT_UNKNOWN
keys.purpose: whether invitations from unknown people may be accepted

keys.name: LINKEDIN_MAX_ACCEPTS_PER_DAY
keys.purpose: daily cap on accepted invitations

keys.name: LINKEDIN_ALLOWED_URLS
keys.purpose: URLs outbound text may contain

keys.name: LINKEDIN_ALLOWED_EMAILS
keys.purpose: emails outbound text may contain

keys.name: LINKEDIN_IDLE_MS
keys.purpose: idle time before the browser closes

keys.name: LINKEDIN_SCREENSHOT
keys.purpose: whether linkedin_screenshot and linkedin_click_at exist; screenshot pixels are not injection-screened (on by default, set false to disable)

keys.name: NAUKRI_SCREENSHOT
keys.purpose: whether naukri_screenshot and naukri_click_at exist; screenshot pixels are not injection-screened (on by default, set false to disable)

keys.name: WELLFOUND_SCREENSHOT
keys.purpose: whether wellfound_screenshot and wellfound_click_at exist; screenshot pixels are not injection-screened (on by default, set false to disable)

keys.name: SCOUT_SCREENSHOT
keys.purpose: whether scout_screenshot and scout_click_at exist; screenshot pixels are not injection-screened (on by default, set false to disable)

steps.explain: Jobber uses a saved browser login for the main LinkedIn account, and a Naukri login. You log in yourself in a real Chrome window that npm run linkedin:login and npm run naukri:login open; passwords and QR codes stay with you.

fixes.sessions: Run the wizard sessions step and log in when the browser window opens, see docs/linkedin-sessions-setup.md and docs/naukri-session-setup.md.
fixes.linkedin.chrome-installed: Install Google Chrome, then run the doctor again.
fixes.linkedin.patchright-importable: Run npm ci in the project in your own terminal.

steps.title: Base resume
steps.explain: The base resume is the one document every tailored resume starts from. It lives in user-data/ and you provide it through the wizard; this guide never reads it.

fixes.resume-valid: Run the wizard resume step to provide or fix the base resume.

steps.title: Profile, languages and job sources
steps.explain: The profile holds the answers used in applications and the languages you really speak. Languages stay a warning until you confirm them. This guide only explains the files; it never opens user-data/.

fixes.profile-valid: Run the wizard profile step and complete the questions.
fixes.languages-confirmed: Review the languages in the wizard profile step and confirm them.

steps.title: Limits, scheduler and automation

keys.name: MATCH_THRESHOLD

keys.name: SEND_LIMIT_PER_RUN

keys.name: MAX_APPLIES_PER_DAY

keys.name: MAX_LINKEDIN_SEARCHES_PER_DAY

keys.name: APPLY_MAX_PER_HOST

keys.name: FOLLOWUPS_AUTONOMOUS

keys.name: FOLLOWUP_CHECK_MAX_AGE_MIN

keys.name: SCHEDULER_ENABLED

keys.name: SCHEDULER_TMUX_SESSION
keys.purpose: tmux session of the wake windows

keys.name: RUN_MAX_WALL_SEC
keys.purpose: time budget per wake

keys.name: RUN_MAX_TOKENS_APPROX
keys.purpose: token budget per wake

keys.name: INBOX_EVERY_MIN
keys.purpose: minutes between inbox sweeps

keys.name: NAUKRI_DISCOVER_EVERY_HOURS
keys.purpose: hours between Naukri discover runs

keys.name: WELLFOUND_DISCOVER_EVERY_HOURS
keys.purpose: hours between Wellfound discover runs

keys.name: USAGE_LIMIT_BACKOFF_MIN
keys.purpose: pause after a subscription usage limit

keys.name: JOBBER_DRY_RUN
keys.purpose: the one dry-run flag: true keeps everything in dry run (and denies Gmail send), false or removed means LIVE

keys.name: JOBBER_KILL
keys.purpose: 1 stops every wake

keys.name: JOBBER_NOTIFY_CMD
keys.purpose: optional command run for owner notices

keys.name: AUTO_UPDATE
keys.purpose: lets the scheduler run the update tick

keys.name: AUTO_UPDATE_REMOTE
keys.purpose: git remote the update fetches from

keys.name: AUTO_UPDATE_BRANCH
keys.purpose: branch the update fast-forwards to

keys.name: AUTO_UPDATE_TAG_PATTERN
keys.purpose: optional tag glob for updates

keys.name: AUTO_UPDATE_REQUIRE_SIGNED
keys.purpose: require signed commits for updates

keys.name: AUTO_UPDATE_SIGNERS_FILE
keys.purpose: allowed signers file for update signatures

keys.name: AUTO_UPDATE_REVIEW_PATHS
keys.purpose: paths that force a manual review

keys.name: BACKUP_ENABLED
keys.purpose: lets the scheduler run the backup tick

keys.name: BACKUP_DIR
keys.purpose: backup destination outside the project

keys.name: BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT
keys.purpose: age public key backups are encrypted to

keys.name: BACKUP_INCLUDE_SECRETS
keys.purpose: whether secrets/ is archived

keys.name: BACKUP_RCLONE_REMOTE
keys.purpose: optional rclone mirror

keys.name: BACKUP_RETAIN_DAILY
keys.purpose: daily archives kept

keys.name: BACKUP_RETAIN_WEEKLY
keys.purpose: weekly archives kept

keys.name: BACKUP_RETAIN_MONTHLY
keys.purpose: monthly archives kept

steps.explain: Limits keep sending slow and safe. The shipped .env.example has JOBBER_DRY_RUN=true (dry run); you turn it off yourself by setting false or removing the line (an unset flag runs LIVE). Show today's numbers with npm run status -- limits; the catalog in src/setup/limitsCatalog.ts is the source, so no numbers are invented here.

fixes.env-limits: Open .env in your own editor and correct the limit named in the doctor line.
fixes.env-inline-comments: Remove the trailing comment from the .env line named in the doctor output.
fixes.scheduler-dry-run: JOBBER_DRY_RUN=true in .env is the dry state; only you decide when to turn it off (false or removed means LIVE).
fixes.dry-run-legacy-keys: Open .env in your own editor and delete the retired SCHEDULER, LINKEDIN, WEB, APPLY and SCOUT dry-run lines named in the doctor output: they are ignored, JOBBER_DRY_RUN is the only dry-run flag.
fixes.scheduler-stop-file: The stop file is the kill switch; only you remove it, with npm run jobber:control -- resume.
fixes.auto-update-config: Updates ship off; leave them off unless you have read docs/backup-and-restore.md.
fixes.backup-config: Backups ship off; follow docs/backup-and-restore.md if you want them.

steps.title: Permission set and hooks

keys.name: WEB_CHAT_ENABLED
keys.purpose: turns on the dashboard chat box (keep off)

keys.name: WEB_APPLY_REQUEST_ENABLED
keys.purpose: turns on the dashboard apply request box (queues one request per confirmed URL; keep off unless you use it)

steps.explain: A permission set decides what a Claude session may do. read_only sends nothing and is the safe default; keep it unless you have a reason. Changing the set is your own command, never the guide.

fixes.permission-set: Check the current set with npm run permissions -- --status; keep read_only unless you decide otherwise in your own terminal.
fixes.project-hooks: Restore .claude/settings.json from git; the safety hooks must be registered.
fixes.gitignore: Restore .gitignore from git so secrets and user data stay untracked.

steps.title: Prompt-injection classifier model

keys.name: CLASSIFIER_MODEL
keys.purpose: profile id of the one active injection classifier; live LinkedIn and Naukri calls fail closed without it

keys.name: SCHEDULER_NO_CLASSIFIER
keys.purpose: skips the classifier for dry runs only

steps.explain: Text from LinkedIn and Naukri is screened by a local model before the agent sees it. The model is downloaded once, pinned and fitted. Without it, live reads and sends are refused by design.

fixes.classifier_model: Fetch and pin the model with the wizard classifier step, see docs/classifier-models.md.
fixes.classifier_smoke: Run npm run models -- verify, then repeat the wizard classifier step if it fails.
fixes.classifier_wired: Restore the surfaces list in the code from git; this is a code problem, not a setting.

keys.name: WEB_PORT

keys.name: WEB_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET

steps.explain: The dashboard is a local page for looking at the funnel. It listens on your own machine only, and sign-in is by default a one-time access token that is shown once and only its hash is stored. Google desktop sign-in or OIDC with one Google account you choose are options.

fixes.web: Start the dashboard with npm run web in your own terminal, see docs/dashboard-exposure.md.
fixes.dashboard-login: In token mode run npm run dashboard -- token in your own terminal to create the access token; in the other modes run the wizard dashboard step to set the allowed account; see docs/dashboard-exposure.md for login recovery.

steps.skip: Skippable (RECOMMENDED). If skipped: no status page in a browser; the limits, working and health commands and npm run status still work. Doctor shows web and dashboard-login as skipped.

steps.title: Final check and dry run
steps.explain: The last stage reruns the doctor and then a dry run that reports PASS or FAIL per stage. Nothing is sent in a dry run. Going live is your own decision, made in your own terminal. When the dry run is clean, the owner starts the stack with npm start (the same as npm run up) and stops it with npm stop (the same as npm run down).

skip_facts: The owner may skip the telegram, dashboard, gmail and apikeys steps in the wizard.
A skip doctor line for a skipped feature is expected and not a problem.
Say what the owner loses (the step's skip text) and name npm run setup -- --step <id> to turn it back on.
The guide never skips anything for the owner and cannot run the wizard.
